evidence_quotes: Nikolski, Alaska and Tobelo, Indonesia led all regions with 8 events each, followed by Mohr, Iran and La Tirana, Chile (6 each)
shallow events (under 10 km depth) were recorded near Mohr, Iran (M4.1 at 1.9 km, M4.9 at 8.5 km), Tual, Indonesia (M4.8 at 2.0 km), and off Honshu, Japan (M5.2 at 2.7 km)
Monitor closely: The Tobelo–Banda Sea corridor and the Mohr, Iran cluster for aftershock escalation; any event exceeding M6.5 in these zones should trigger immediate reassessment
the late-period uptick (Feb 13–15 combined: 22 events) may indicate a building sequence
criticisms: No explicit 24-hour action items are provided — the report never tells a coordinator to 'alert county X', 'contact USGS for a focal mechanism review on the Mohr cluster', or 'verify shelter capacity near Tobelo'. The closest it gets is 'monitor closely', which is not decision-grade.
The M6.5 threshold trigger is useful but framed as a future condition, not an immediate action. There is no instruction on what to do right now with the existing M6.1 maximum event.
La Tirana, Chile is listed as a top-activity region (6 events) but receives no follow-up risk framing or monitoring priority — it disappears after the bullet listing it.

No distinction is made between regions where US/state-level coordinators have jurisdiction or mutual-aid obligations (Alaska) versus international zones — this matters for resource pre-positioning decisions.
The 'broad, simultaneous fault-system stress' claim is speculative and not actionable; it could be cut in favor of a concrete recommendation.
